title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #5

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What should you find first when you read a map? (1 mark)
   A. The north arrow
   B. The colours
   C. The size of the paper
   D. The names of rivers

2. Which direction is Mombasa from Nairobi on a map of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. North
   C. North-west
   D. South-east

3. A pupil faces the rising sun in the morning. Which direction is on the pupil's left hand? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. East
   C. South
   D. West

4. Which imaginary line crosses Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The river line
   B. The equator
   C. The railway line
   D. The boundary

5. What is a neighbouring county? (1 mark)
   A. A county with the same name
   B. The biggest county
   C. A county that shares a boundary with your county
   D. A county in another country

6. What is a plain? (1 mark)
   A. A waterfall
   B. Wide flat land
   C. A lake with salt water
   D. A steep mountain

7. Which of these is built by people, not natural? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A plain
   C. A hill
   D. A dam

8. Which drink is likely to sell more during the hot season? (1 mark)
   A. Cold drinks
   B. Hot porridge
   C. Hot soup
   D. Hot tea

9. Which clothing helps drivers to see you on a rainy day? (1 mark)
   A. Black clothes
   B. Bright or reflective clothes
   C. Dark grey clothes
   D. Brown clothes

10. Which of these is most likely to happen in the rainy season? (1 mark)
   A. Grass dries up completely
   B. Rivers fill with water
   C. Herders move very far for water
   D. Farmers harvest all their maize

11. What is a monument? (1 mark)
   A. A market
   B. A bus
   C. A structure built to remember a person or event
   D. A river

12. In a chart of who gives and who needs, what does a nurse give? (1 mark)
   A. Learning
   B. Food
   C. Transport
   D. Health care

13. What is barter? (1 mark)
   A. Giving things away
   B. Exchanging one thing for another without money
   C. Buying with money only
   D. Stealing

14. Which is a reason why many people live in towns? (1 mark)
   A. No water
   B. No roads
   C. Jobs, shops and services
   D. No schools

15. What does population distribution mean? (1 mark)
   A. How many trees are in an area
   B. How much rain falls
   C. How tall the mountains are
   D. How people are spread out in an area

16. What is the history of a school? (1 mark)
   A. The school timetable
   B. The school menu
   C. The story of how it started and changed
   D. The school bell

17. What is discipline? (1 mark)
   A. Running away
   B. Shouting
   C. Doing what you like
   D. Controlling yourself and following rules

18. Which national park in Narok County is famous for wildlife? (1 mark)
   A. Maasai Mara
   B. Nakuru town
   C. Kakamega
   D. Lake Victoria

19. Which of these is a safe way for a child to take part in economic activities? (1 mark)
   A. Working at night
   B. Helping in the school garden
   C. Carrying heavy loads all day
   D. Working in a quarry

20. Which is a way of conserving water? (1 mark)
   A. Polluting rivers
   B. Turning off taps after use
   C. Leaving taps running
   D. Cutting trees near rivers

21. Which is an agro-based industry? (1 mark)
   A. A school
   B. A bank
   C. A tea factory
   D. A hotel

22. What is a product? (1 mark)
   A. A tool
   B. A finished good that is made
   C. A worker
   D. A raw material

23. Who keeps the money and records it in a school project? (1 mark)
   A. The visitor
   B. The treasurer
   C. The gatekeeper
   D. The safety officer

24. Who should handle sharp tools in a school project? (1 mark)
   A. A visitor
   B. Nobody
   C. An adult
   D. A young child alone

25. Which information should you not share with strangers online? (1 mark)
   A. The weather
   B. The name of your favourite fruit
   C. A joke
   D. Your home address and password

26. Which of these spoils peace? (1 mark)
   A. Forgiveness
   B. Listening
   C. Bullying
   D. Fairness

27. What is peace? (1 mark)
   A. A loud noise
   B. A game
   C. A kind of food
   D. Calm and harmony where people live safely and respect each other

28. What is bullying? (1 mark)
   A. Repeatedly hurting or frightening someone weaker
   B. Playing together
   C. Helping a friend
   D. Sharing food

29. What does fairness mean? (1 mark)
   A. Favouring friends
   B. Favouring rich people
   C. Ignoring people
   D. Treating everyone equally

30. What is a right? (1 mark)
   A. A chore
   B. A game
   C. Something every person is allowed to have or do
   D. A punishment

31. Which school transport is safe? (1 mark)
   A. A stranger's car
   B. A vehicle approved by school and parents
   C. An overloaded vehicle
   D. A vehicle with no seats

32. What is campaigning? (1 mark)
   A. Counting votes
   B. Announcing results
   C. Telling voters why they should choose you
   D. Throwing away ballots

33. Which shows respect for the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Insulting leaders
   B. Ignoring leaders
   C. Laughing at them
   D. Following fair instructions politely

34. Why is a Children's Government important? (1 mark)
   A. It gives pupils a voice and shares responsibility
   B. It closes the school
   C. It punishes children
   D. It stops learning

35. What is an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. A game
   B. A sports match
   C. A kind of food
   D. A list of items to be discussed at a meeting

36. Which is the right way to make a complaint? (1 mark)
   A. By shouting in class
   B. By spreading rumours
   C. By fighting
   D. Through your class representative

37. What is a community? (1 mark)
   A. A type of crop
   B. A group of people who live in the same area and share things
   C. A school subject
   D. A kind of animal

38. Which of these leads prayers in a mosque? (1 mark)
   A. A nurse
   B. An imam
   C. A cook
   D. A tailor

39. Which quality means treating everyone equally? (1 mark)
   A. Selfishness
   B. Greed
   C. Fairness
   D. Boasting

40. Why do we have county governments? (1 mark)
   A. To close schools
   B. To bring services closer to the people
   C. To end services
   D. To stop elections

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three reasons why people need directions in everyday life. (3 marks)

42. Design a poster: write a slogan and list three qualities of a good leader you would show on it. (5 marks)

43. Explain why we should be honest even when nobody is watching. (3 marks)

44. Draw a weather chart for three days: sunny, rainy, cloudy. Add a key. (3 marks)

45. State the direction that is opposite to each of these: north and east. (2 marks)

46. Name four forms of child abuse. (4 marks)

47. Explain why a monument is built. (2 marks)

48. Give three qualities of a good leader and explain why each matters. (3 marks)

49. Give four school rules and one reason for each. (4 marks)

50. Explain why herding communities live in sparsely populated areas. (3 marks)

51. Explain why children must not be forced to do hard work. (3 marks)

52. Give three examples of artefacts and say how each is used. (3 marks)

53. Explain how you can find east in the morning without a compass. (2 marks)

54. Explain what devolution means. (2 marks)

55. Give two examples of goods and two examples of services. (4 marks)

56. State three benefits of democracy in school. (3 marks)

57. Describe how you would make a poster on an economic activity in your county. (4 marks)

58. Draw a compass rose and label the four cardinal points. (3 marks)

59. Explain the difference between a right and a duty and give one example of each in school. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — The north arrow
   Finding north first helps you read all other directions.

2. D — South-east
   Mombasa lies to the south-east of Nairobi.

3. A — North
   Facing east, north is on the left and south is on the right.

4. B — The equator
   The equator crosses the middle of Kenya.

5. C — A county that shares a boundary with your county
   Neighbouring counties touch each other along a boundary.

6. B — Wide flat land
   A plain is a wide, flat area.

7. D — A dam
   A dam is built by people to hold water.

8. A — Cold drinks
   People are thirsty and feel hot, so they buy cold drinks.

9. B — Bright or reflective clothes
   Bright and reflective clothes stand out.

10. B — Rivers fill with water
   Rain fills rivers and streams.

11. C — A structure built to remember a person or event
   Monuments remind people of important people or events.

12. D — Health care
   Nurses give health care.

13. B — Exchanging one thing for another without money
   Barter means swapping goods, such as a goat for grain.

14. C — Jobs, shops and services
   Towns offer work and services.

15. D — How people are spread out in an area
   Distribution is about where people live.

16. C — The story of how it started and changed
   History tells how the school began and grew.

17. D — Controlling yourself and following rules
   Discipline is self-control and obeying rules.

18. A — Maasai Mara
   The Maasai Mara is in Narok County.

19. B — Helping in the school garden
   Light safe work under supervision is fine.

20. B — Turning off taps after use
   Saving water helps everyone.

21. C — A tea factory
   Agro-based industries use farm produce.

22. B — A finished good that is made
   Products are the goods that come out of a factory.

23. B — The treasurer
   The treasurer handles and records money.

24. C — An adult
   Adults must handle dangerous tools.

25. D — Your home address and password
   Private details must be kept safe.

26. C — Bullying
   Bullying hurts and frightens people.

27. D — Calm and harmony where people live safely and respect each other
   Peace is harmony and safety.

28. A — Repeatedly hurting or frightening someone weaker
   Bullying is repeated unkind behaviour.

29. D — Treating everyone equally
   Fair people give everyone equal treatment.

30. C — Something every person is allowed to have or do
   Rights protect people.

31. B — A vehicle approved by school and parents
   Approved vehicles are safer.

32. C — Telling voters why they should choose you
   Candidates campaign before elections.

33. D — Following fair instructions politely
   Respect includes obeying fair instructions.

34. A — It gives pupils a voice and shares responsibility
   It teaches leadership and democracy.

35. D — A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
   An agenda gives the order of business.

36. D — Through your class representative
   Use proper channels.

37. B — A group of people who live in the same area and share things
   People in a community share a market, a school or customs.

38. B — An imam
   An imam leads prayers.

39. C — Fairness
   Fair leaders treat all equally.

40. B — To bring services closer to the people
   Counties bring services near to people.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: To find places, to travel safely, and to explain to others where something is. Accept sailors, pilots and farmers using direction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: A slogan such as A Good Leader Serves, and qualities such as honest, fair and kind, with a picture.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a slogan, 3 marks for three qualities, 1 mark for a picture.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty builds trust, it is right, and it prepares us to be good citizens.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Three boxes with a sun, a cloud with rain lines and a plain cloud, and a key that names each symbol.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for correct symbols, 1 mark for the days, 1 mark for the key.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: The opposite of north is south. The opposite of east is west.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct opposite.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Early and forced marriage, female genital mutilation, child labour and child trafficking. Accept slavery, sexual abuse, abuse of children with special needs or unsafe transport.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each form.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: A monument is built to remind people of an important person or event so that they remember it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reminding people, 1 mark for the idea of a person or event.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty so people trust the leader, fairness so all are treated equally, and listening so decisions are wise.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality with reason.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Come on time to avoid missing lessons; keep the school clean for health; respect others for peace; care for property so it lasts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule with a reason.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: The land is dry, so it cannot support many farms. Herders move with their animals to look for water and grass. So only a few people stay in one place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: It harms their health, it stops them going to school, and it is child labour, which is against the law.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: A clay pot for cooking or storing water, a basket for carrying items, and a stool for sitting. Accept other correct examples.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct artefact with use.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Face the direction where the sun rises. That direction is east.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using the rising sun, 1 mark for naming east.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means sharing power and resources between the national government and county governments.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharing power, 1 mark for national and county.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Goods: maize and shoes. Services: teaching and nursing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone has a voice, decisions are fair, and pupils obey rules they helped to make.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose one activity, draw a large picture showing people at work, write a title and two or three facts, and add one way of conserving the resource.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with N at the top, E on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for neat drawing, 1 mark for N at top, 1 mark for E, S and W correct.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: A right is something you are allowed, such as learning in a safe place. A duty is something you must do, such as following the rules.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each example.
